Maya: ran a quick nsys+perfetto pass on the 4xA100 inference job, pushed the trace to perfetto — need eyes on kernel hotspots :eyes:
Devin: link? did you capture sm_efficiency + l1/gmem metrics?
Maya: perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (shortlink)
Maya: nsys command: `nsys profile --trace=cuda --metrics sm_efficiency,gld_throughput,gst_inst,dram__throughput --output profile_1819`
Maya: top-line kernel ranking from the summary (total GPU time):
```
Kernel                       calls   total_ms  avg_ms  %time  sm_eff
multi_head_attention_fwd     128     312.4     2.44    42.3   22%
kv_cache_read_kernel         2048    150.6     0.073   20.4   11%
sgemm_128x64                 512     120.1     0.23    16.3   68%
softmax_forward              256     85.3      0.33    11.6   45%
zero_memset                  1024    41.0      0.04    5.5    3%
apply_rotary                 2000    28.7      0.014   3.9    35%
```
Maya: notes: MHA consumes ~42% and has very low sm_eff — looks memory bound. kv_cache_read_kernel has huge call count (lots of tiny launches) and only ~11% sm_eff. sgemm has good sm_eff but still large wall time. zero_memset is suspicious for being high-frequency tiny operations.
Devin: the kv reads smell like launch overhead + uncoalesced loads. what's batch size / seq len distribution?
Maya: batch=1, beam=1, variable seq lengths (mostly 12-64). decode loop triggers many tiny kv reads per token.
Sasha: if batch=1 that's expected. try batching prefix KV reads across beams or coalescing requests before calling GPU. also check if prefetching is disabled — that increases kernel counts.
Kevin: zero_memset at 5% could be coming from buffer-clear in the decode hot loop. Switching to cudaMemsetAsync on a worker-specific stream might hide cost. Also consider reusing buffers instead of clearing every token.
Anika: for sgemm: since sm_eff is high, it's compute-bound. We can try cublasLt/epilogue fuse or quantized matmul to reduce time; I'll prototype int8 path.
Devin: can you re-run with `nsys profile --sample=10us --trace=cuda --metrics sm_efficiency,gld_throughput,gst_inst,dram__throughput --output profile_1819_sample` and include `--duration` for a 30s steady window? that'll give better sampling for hot loops.
Maya: will do. also rerunning with `--kernels-only` gave clearer kernel timeline — lots of small kernels around decode boundary.
Sasha: another angle: KV-cache read kernel low sm_eff could be due to heavy divergence from varying seqlen masks. If we batch by sequence length buckets we get fewer divergent warps and better occupancy.
Kevin: we should also check register pressure — if kernels are spilling, occupancy drops. capture `registers_per_thread` / local memory in the next run or use nvprof/cupti to sample.
Maya: noted. next runs to include `smsp__active_cycles_sm` and register metrics.
Anika: I'll take sgemm tuning, Sasha can try batching/coalescing, Kevin can look at memset/stream reuse. Maya, drop the new traces into the perf folder and ping this thread when done. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Canary deployment 2026-03-12T14:33:07Z — inference service v2.7 -> succeeded
Devin: quick wins list: 1) coalesce KV reads (reduce calls) 2) fuse/async memset 3) sequence-length bucketing 4) try cublasLt int8 for sgemm 5) rerun sampling metrics
Maya: thanks — splitting work and will iterate on PRs. will post perf diffs once we have the new traces.
Kevin: one more thing — watch out for kernel launch serialization from stream syncs in the host loop. small kernels + syncs = CPU-side bottleneck.
Maya: good call, I'll grep for `cudaDeviceSynchronize` in decode path and remove where unnecessary.
